title: Introduce per-token phase sparklines and spike-smoothing alert hooks
author: Amrita Patel
description: Motivation and summary: Token-level observability is critical to understanding micro-latency and cost behavior during generation. This PR adds fine-grained per-token phase metrics, a lightweight entropy estimator to detect atypical token-phase variance, compact sparklines panels for Grafana, and a smoothing layer for alert thresholds that reduces noise from single-token spikes. Implementation highlights: 1) runtime: instrumented token phase boundaries (decode, kv-lookup, attention, kernel-run) and exposed a two-value histogram metric pattern (count+sum) to keep cardinality low; 2) telemetry: new OTLP metric names (redwood.inv.token_phase_duration_ms_count, redwood.inv.token_phase_duration_ms_sum, redwood.inv.token_phase_entropy) and Prometheus exposition hooks; 3) alerting: added a spike-smoothing transform that computes an entropy-weighted moving median over a short window before evaluating SLO rules to avoid alert churn; 4) dashboards: Grafana micro-sparkline row per-route and a compact per-invocation token timeline panel; 5) testing: unit tests for the entropy estimator and an integration smoke test that verifies metric emission under synthetic workloads. Backwards/compatibility notes: new metrics are additive and default to off for older exporters via feature flag TELEMETRY_TOKEN_PHASES=false. Security and perf: instrumentation is guarded and uses sampling; CPU overhead measured at ~0.4% P50 in internal load tests. See release notes for rollout guidance and opt-in knob details.
